subject: Failover traces, sample RPO timing, and gap analysis
messages:
From: David Reynolds <david.reynolds@novapay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: NovaPay Security Team <security@novapay.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: RPO/RTO evidence: traces + sample timings

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our compliance team had two follow-ups after reviewing your SOC/SIG packet: we need (1) a short set of representative failover traces (kernel-level timestamps or server-side logs) showing a warm-start failover sequence, and (2) a tight list of measured RPO/RTO numbers from your last quarterly rehearsal with supporting artifacts.

Specifically, can you provide:
- a 2–5 minute snippet from the warm cache failover showing KV cache load times, prefix-warm signals, and the first successful token emission. Ideally with timestamps in ISO and pod IDs.
- the RPO/RTO summary table used in the audit (minute-level values) and the run notes that indicate any manual steps.
- an explanation of how quantized model variants affect recovery time (if any).

We prefer artifacts as simple log excerpts or CSVs rather than large zip files. Also, please include any mitigation steps you take when a cache-warm isn't possible (cold boot path) and approximate extra latency/tokens lost in that scenario.

If you can send by EOD Friday (PST) we can include them in our SIG submission.

Thanks,
David
David Reynolds
Senior Security Analyst, NovaPay
security@novapay.com

Attachment stubs referenced: warm_start_trace_20270519.log (requested snippet), rto_test_summary_20270515.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Reynolds <david.reynolds@novapay.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RPO/RTO evidence: traces + sample timings

Hi David —

Thanks — attaching the requested excerpts. Quick summary up front so your reviewers can find the key bits:

1) warm_start_trace_20270519.log (attached) — 2.8 minute snippet from our controlled warm-start failover test on 2027-05-19. Includes per-pod timestamps, KV cache restore start/end, and first-token emission marker. You27ll see the sequence we described on the call (leader re-election -> cache rehydration -> prefix warm signal -> first token).

2) rto_test_summary_20270515.pdf (attached) — the table your team wanted. Row format: test_id, date, region, pod_count, measured_RPO_minutes, measured_RTO_seconds, notes. Our typical warm-start RTO (median) is ~7.6s; 95th percentile 18.9s in the test matrix when KV cache hit-rate >= 82%. Cold-start paths (cache miss) show RTOs of 72s median. RPO for our streaming workload is < 2 minutes for all tests we retain.

3) kv-cache-hitrates.csv (attached) — per-test hit-ratio snapshots used to correlate RTO variance.

How quantized variants matter: quantization changes model size and memory load times. In practice, the 8-bit quantized variants reduce rehydration time ~12–20% versus 16-bit in our environment, primarily because there27s less data to stream during KV restore. We note that for very short-lived bursts the difference is smaller because kernel scheduling dominates.

Mitigation when a warm cache is not possible: we have three controls — (a) fallback to a smaller compatible model variant pinned in the routing policy (adds 5–12% latency), (b) opportunistic prefix-caching from recent requests (best-effort), and (c) traffic-weighted standby pool (reserved capacity) that can take overflow in severe cases.

I27ve uploaded the full runbook excerpt and the test logs to the shared Drive link below and included the attachment stubs in this thread. If your team wants raw JSON lines from the trace we can produce them but I kept the attached log snippet human-readable.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novapay/rpo-runbook-v2

Attaching: warm_start_trace_20270519.log, rto_test_summary_20270515.pdf, kv-cache-hitrates.csv

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, David Reynolds <david.reynolds@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RPO/RTO evidence: traces + sample timings

Kim / David —

Adding a few granular numbers from the infra side to contextualize the log:
- KV cache rehydrate: median 2.4s (pod-wide), 95th 6.3s when the backing store requires multiple shard loads.
- First-token emission after rehydrate: median 5.2s.
- Observed token-delivery tail in one noisy test: 34s (that case had S3 throttling during artifact fetch; we included the incident note in the PDF).

Also worth calling out: our prefix warm heuristic kicks in for sequences with a historical probability threshold >0.12; when that heuristic triggers, the warm path RTO improves ~35% because we prefetch top-K KV entries during leader election. The attached CSV shows hit-rates versus measured RTO.

If NovaPay27s reviewers need canonical timestamps in RFC3339 per-line rather than our current human-friendly format, we can re-export.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: David Reynolds <david.reynolds@novapay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: NovaPay Security Team <security@novapay.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RPO/RTO evidence: traces + sample timings

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed.

Two small asks before we close the SIG entry: (1) can you add a one-paragraph attestation line we can include in the questionnaire that confirms the retention policy for these test artifacts (how long you keep raw traces and where), and (2) if possible re-export the log with RFC3339 timestamps for line-level correlation with our ingestion records.

If you can send those two items early next week that will get us green across the RPO/RTO section. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Thanks,
David
Senior Security Analyst, NovaPay
